meaning:
κληρονομία, -ας, ἡ
(κληρονόμος) [in LXX chiefly for נַחֲלָה, also for יְרֻשָּׁה, etc. ;]
prop., an inherited property, an inheritance: Mat.21:38, Mrk.12:7, Luk.12:13 20:14; in general, a possession, inheritance: Act.7:5, Heb.11:8; of the Messianic Kingdom and its blessings, Act.20:32, Gal.3:18, Col.3:24, Eph.1:14, 18 5:5, Heb.9:15, 1Pe.1:4.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: But the farmers, when they saw the son, said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him, and seize his inheritance.’
But those farmers said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
One of the multitude said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”
He gave him no inheritance in it, no, not so much as to set his foot on. He promised that he would give it to him for a possession, and to his offspring after…
For if the inheritance is of the law, it is no more of promise; but God has granted it to Abraham by promise.
who is a pledge of our inheritance, to the redemption of God’s own possession, to the praise of his glory.
knowing that from the Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance; for you serve the Lord Christ.
For this reason he is the mediator of a new covenant, since a death has occurred for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first covenant…
